title: Daily Market Digest - October 22, 2026
subtitle: Risk-Off Sentiment Dominates as AI Doubts and Oil Surge Weigh on Markets

items.headline: U.S. Equities Trade Lower Amid Renewed AI Concerns and Surging Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. stock markets are experiencing a broad risk-off sentiment on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Doubts surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) spending, coupled with escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East driving crude oil prices higher, are contributing to a cautious investor mood. Technology stocks, in particular, are facing downward pressure.

items.headline: Super Micro Computer Inc. ($SMCI) surges on strong guidance
items.summary: Shares of Super Micro Computer Inc. jumped 9.6% after the AI server manufacturer significantly raised its first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue projection, signaling robust demand in the AI sector.

items.headline: QuantumScape ($QS) climbs after narrower Q3 loss
items.summary: QuantumScape shares surged 8% after the solid-state battery developer reported a narrower Q3 net loss of $84.5 million, or $0.14 per share, surpassing year-ago figures.

items.headline: Kinder Morgan ($KMI) rises on strong Q3 results and pipeline projects
items.summary: Kinder Morgan shares climbed 3% after reporting better-than-expected Q3 results and announcing final investment decisions for two major Permian natural gas pipeline projects, boosting its backlog by $4.7 billion.

items.headline: IBM ($IBM) declines despite raised software revenue forecast
items.summary: IBM fell 4.7% today, despite the company raising its annual software revenue forecast and reporting third-quarter results ahead of Wall Street expectations, caught in the broader risk-off sentiment.

items.headline: American Airlines ($AAL) drops on annual loss forecast due to fuel costs
items.summary: American Airlines shares dropped 3.2% after forecasting an annual loss, despite setting new revenue records in Q3 2026, as high jet fuel prices continue to squeeze margins.

items.headline: Tesla ($TSLA) slides after cutting capital expenditure forecast
items.summary: Tesla shares slid today after the company announced a reduction in its annual capital expenditure forecast, contributing to a broader sell-off in growth stocks amidst renewed doubts over AI spending.

items.headline: Technology and Cyclical Sectors Under Pressure as Risk-Off Mood Intensifies
items.summary: A prevalent risk-off sentiment is impacting the market, with technology and cyclical sectors experiencing heavier selling. Professional funds have notably been selling technology stocks, a trend observed roughly once a decade. While some defensive sectors showed relative resilience in the prior session, the overall market weakness today suggests widespread caution across various industries.

items.headline: Light Economic Data Schedule; Fed Remains in Blackout Period
items.summary: The U.S. economic calendar is light today, with releases including weekly jobless claims, September leading and coincident indicators, and the Kansas City Fed's October manufacturing survey. The Federal Reserve remains in its blackout period ahead of next week's FOMC meeting, scheduled for October 27-28.

items.headline: Brent Crude Jumps Over 2.8% Amid Heightened Middle East Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude surged more than 2.8% to $111.92 a barrel, nearing a five-month high. This jump is attributed to heightened fears of supply disruptions stemming from escalating Middle East conflict and further Houthi attacks. The rise in crude prices is adding to market jitters and concerns over inflation.

items.headline: Mixed Reactions to Q3 Earnings from Major Companies
items.summary: The third-quarter earnings season continues with key companies reporting results. Lockheed Martin ($LMT) announced an 11% increase in Q3 sales to $20.7 billion and a record backlog of $292.0 billion. Nasdaq ($NDAQ) reported a 13% rise in Q3 net revenue to $1.5 billion. Allegion ($ALLE) saw a 9.6% revenue increase and raised its full-year outlook. In contrast, American Airlines ($AAL) dropped after forecasting an annual loss due to high fuel costs, despite achieving new revenue records. Blackstone ($BX) also edged lower following its quarterly earnings report.
